questions.q: A writer's ensemble drama has five siblings but no one the audience should root for. What keeps it gripping, in the Succession model?
choices: Giving one sibling a save-the-cat moment so we have a hero
Rotating focus and sympathy, so the question becomes who betrays whom
Adding a narrator who tells us whom to trust
Cutting to two siblings, since ensembles can't hold suspense
questions.explain: With no hero, Succession hands the centre to different characters and makes whoever is losing the one we feel for.

questions.q: How does Armstrong say Succession's actors should play its comedy?
choices: Broadly, signalling the joke to the audience
As improvised sketches loosely attached to the plot
As real: the laughs come from characters taking themselves seriously
Directly to camera, as in Peep Show
questions.explain: In a Backstage interview he said the cast has to play everything as real.

questions.q: Roman makes a crude joke whenever someone close to him is hurt. What's the best reading of the scene?
choices: The insult is armour: look for what he's protecting
It's comic relief, unrelated to his character
It's exposition about the company
It's a sign the writers improvised the scene
questions.explain: The Roys rarely say what they feel; insults and deflection carry it as subtext.

choices: Alternative endings shot for each season finale
Actors' fully improvised scenes replacing the script
Alternative casting for each role
Alternative lines written shortly before shooting for moments that could be funnier or truer
questions.explain: Armstrong and the writers marked spots in a scripted scene and supplied options for actors to try in different takes.

questions.q: A season of your ensemble series has many separate schemes. What does Succession's season shape suggest?
choices: End each episode on a cliffhanger and leave the season open
Bring everyone to one family occasion where the schemes converge and a betrayal turns the power
Resolve one scheme per episode, like a procedural
Save every reveal for a flashback episode
questions.explain: Weddings, a yacht trip and a board vote gather the whole cast in one place where they must choose sides.

questions.q: Why, according to Armstrong, did Logan's death in season 4 happen without a death scene?
choices: The actor wasn't available
HBO's rules on violence
It was deliberate: the episode is about the children's reactions
To leave open whether he really died
questions.explain: We hear it through phones, at second hand, because the point is who each child is without him.

questions.q: In 'Hunting', Logan makes his executives crawl and fight over sausages. Which idea is the scene built on?
choices: Dialogue as a status contest: who will humiliate themselves, and who will humiliate others to stay safe
The hero's journey's ordeal
A withheld backstory revealed
The rule of three
questions.explain: The whole scene is about rank, the same contest that drives Succession's dialogue.

ideas: An ensemble can work with no hero at all, if every member wants the same thing and pursues it with a different weapon.
Write alternative lines just before shooting so actors can try a funnier or truer version inside a scripted scene.
A writers' room is for breaking stories and planning the season, not for writing the scripts.
Comedy and tragedy can be the same scene, as long as the actors play it entirely as real.
